answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow thaw: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after a long, verifiable service history, so a new identity starts with almost no trust. Like crossing a frozen tundra, an attacker must spend real time and funds for every fake agent, while honest agents build standing on a small knoll of proven work. When many identities suddenly appear from one delta of funding, the network flags the cluster and demands fresh proof of unique work, making a sybil flood cost far more than any reward it could harvest.
